head_commit.message: docs(node): record verified automatic recovery boundaries

fix(server): retire sessions on re-login, scope key revocation and email sync

Three lifecycle rules from docs/v2 that the implementation only approximated:

- Re-login (enrollment with `existing`) always ends the Node's previous
  control sessions, open demands and instance, even when the configured
  identity did not change. Previously this depended on the configuration
  commit detecting an identity/binding diff, so a same-identity re-login left
  the old session valid. `retire_node_sessions` is now shared by the commit
  effects and the PKCE redeem path.

- Revoking a key only withdraws the Node's execution when that key was still
  the current generation and not yet revoked. Revoking a retired generation,
  or repeating a revocation, records nothing new and no longer tears down
  targets established with the current key. `store::revoke_key` returns
  whether anything changed; the extra pre-check query is gone.

- Email maintenance only visits networks where the user holds an active
  membership and only renames bindings of that membership. Bindings kept by a
  revoked membership stay under the old name, so a former network neither
  learns the new address nor records a maintenance version. `EmailSync`
  carries the membership so the commit participant revalidates the same rule.

Regression coverage: same-identity re-login in
enrollment_key_idempotency_tag_relogin_and_permanent_delete, retired-key
revocation in review_rotation_http_response_loss_recovers_same_keys, and the
departed-member source assertion in
removed_member_references_survive_email_maintenance_and_never_rebind_on_save.
